families.web: Add or fix the security headers and web server settings, then run the scan again to check.
families.tls: Renew the certificate before it expires, enable TLS 1.2 or higher and remove obsolete protocols and cipher suites.
families.email: Publish consistent SPF, DKIM and DMARC records in your domain's DNS, then aim for a strict DMARC policy.
families.dns: Fix the DNS zone at your provider: remove orphaned records and enable DNSSEC if possible.
families.network: Close the ports that do not need to be public and put administration services behind a VPN or a firewall.
families.identity: Check the domain registration details and enable locking and privacy at the registrar.
families.reputation: Find the cause of the poor reputation, fix it, then request removal from the services concerned.
families.leaks: Change the exposed credentials, remove published files or secrets and enable two-factor authentication.

modules.dns_records: Fill in the missing records (A, MX, NS, CAA) and delete the ones no longer used.
modules.subdomains: Delete unused subdomains and make sure each one is protected like the main domain.
modules.security_headers: Add Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy in the web server configuration.
modules.tls_certificate: Renew the certificate before it expires (ideally with automatic renewal) and check that it covers the site name.
modules.technologies: Update the detected components and hide version numbers in the server headers.
modules.geo_data: Check that hosting is in the expected region and that the IP address belongs to your provider.
modules.whois_data: Check the domain contacts, enable transfer lock and plan ahead for the expiry date.
modules.open_ports: Close unnecessary ports at the firewall and restrict administration services (SSH, databases) by IP address or VPN.
modules.email_security: Publish or tighten SPF (-all), DKIM and DMARC (p=quarantine then p=reject), and add MTA-STS if your provider supports it.
modules.waf: Put the site behind a web application firewall (WAF) or a CDN that filters common attacks.
modules.redirect_chain: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS in a single step and avoid chains of multiple redirects.
modules.web_files: Remove publicly accessible sensitive files and review the content of robots.txt and security.txt.
modules.cookie_security: Add the Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes to session cookies.
modules.cors: Replace wildcard allowed origins (*) with the exact list of sites that need to access your API.
modules.reverse_dns: Make the IP address's reverse DNS match the server name, especially for the mail server.
modules.network_extended: Check network ownership (ASN) and BGP announcements, and ask your host to fix any anomaly.
modules.screenshot: Check that the displayed page is the expected one and shows no unexpected content.
modules.subdomain_takeover: Delete the DNS record that points to a service you no longer use, or recreate the resource on that service.

spf.name: SPF
spf.def: DNS record listing the servers allowed to send mail for the domain. It limits sender spoofing.

dkim.name: DKIM
dkim.def: Cryptographic signature added to each outgoing email. The recipient checks it with a key published in DNS.

dmarc.name: DMARC
dmarc.def: Policy that says what to do with an email failing SPF or DKIM (ignore, quarantine, reject) and where to send reports.

bimi.name: BIMI
bimi.def: Lets your brand logo appear in the inbox, provided you have a strict DMARC policy.

mta_sts.name: MTA-STS
mta_sts.def: Policy that forces mail servers to encrypt mail sent to your domain with TLS.

tls_rpt.name: TLS-RPT
tls_rpt.def: Reports sent when a TLS connection to your mail server fails. Complements MTA-STS.

dane.name: DANE
dane.def: Publishes in DNS (protected by DNSSEC) the expected certificate fingerprint, to authenticate a server without relying on an authority.

dnssec.name: DNSSEC
dnssec.def: Cryptographic signing of DNS answers. It prevents name resolutions from being forged or redirected.

caa.name: CAA
caa.def: DNS record restricting which certificate authorities may issue a certificate for your domain.

hsts.name: HSTS
hsts.def: Header that forces the browser to use only HTTPS for your site for a given duration.

csp.name: CSP
csp.def: Header listing the allowed sources for scripts, images and styles. It limits the impact of injection flaws (XSS).

cors.name: CORS
cors.def: Mechanism deciding which other sites may call your API from a browser.

x_frame_options.name: X-Frame-Options
x_frame_options.def: Header that forbids showing your page in a frame of another site, against clickjacking.

referrer_policy.name: Referrer-Policy
referrer_policy.def: Header controlling the originating page address sent to sites visited next.

permissions_policy.name: Permissions-Policy
permissions_policy.def: Header that enables or disables browser features (camera, microphone, location) for your page.

httponly.name: HttpOnly
httponly.def: Cookie attribute that prevents scripts from reading it. It protects sessions against XSS theft.

samesite.name: SameSite
samesite.def: Cookie attribute that limits sending it on requests from another site, against CSRF attacks.

asn.name: ASN
asn.def: Autonomous system number: the network (host, carrier) announcing an IP address on the Internet.

bgp.name: BGP
bgp.def: Protocol by which networks announce the IP addresses they can reach. A wrong announcement can hijack traffic.

ct.name: CT (Certificate Transparency)
ct.def: Public logs where every certificate authority records issued certificates. Useful to spot an unexpected certificate.

ocsp.name: OCSP
ocsp.def: Service used to check that a certificate has not been revoked. OCSP stapling avoids an extra request.

tls.name: TLS
tls.def: Protocol that encrypts connections (HTTPS, mail). Versions 1.2 and 1.3 are the only ones to keep.

certificate.name: Certificat
certificate.def: Digital document proving a site's identity and holding the public key used for encryption.

ca.name: Autorité de certification
ca.def: Trusted organization that signs certificates and guarantees they belong to their holder.

san.name: SAN
san.def: List of domain names covered by a single certificate (Subject Alternative Name).

cipher.name: Suite de chiffrement
cipher.def: Set of algorithms negotiated for a TLS connection. Old suites can be broken.

pfs.name: Confidentialité persistante
pfs.def: Property that protects past exchanges even if the server key is stolen later (Perfect Forward Secrecy).

dns.name: DNS
dns.def: The Internet's directory: it translates a domain name into an IP address and says where to deliver mail.

a_record.name: Enregistrement A
a_record.def: Maps a name to an IPv4 address.

aaaa_record.name: Enregistrement AAAA
aaaa_record.def: Maps a name to an IPv6 address.

mx.name: MX
mx.def: Record naming the mail servers that receive the domain's mail.

ns.name: NS
ns.def: Record naming the authoritative DNS servers for the domain.

txt.name: TXT
txt.def: Free-text record, used for SPF, DMARC, DKIM and ownership checks.

cname.name: CNAME
cname.def: Alias: a name that points to another name. A CNAME to a disabled service exposes you to takeover.

soa.name: SOA
soa.def: Header record of the DNS zone: primary server, contact and refresh timers.

ptr.name: PTR (DNS inverse)
ptr.def: Maps an IP address to a name. Mail servers check it to judge a sender.

ttl.name: TTL
ttl.def: Duration, in seconds, during which a DNS answer may be cached before being asked again.

zone_transfer.name: Transfert de zone
zone_transfer.def: Full copy of the DNS zone (AXFR). Open to everyone, it reveals the list of your machines.

wildcard_dns.name: DNS générique
wildcard_dns.def: Record answering for any nonexistent subdomain. It skews subdomain discovery.

subdomain.name: Sous-domaine
subdomain.def: Name placed in front of your domain (for example mail.example.com), often forgotten and so less monitored.

takeover.name: Prise de contrôle de sous-domaine
takeover.def: A subdomain points to a service you no longer use: a third party can claim it and publish in your name.

waf.name: WAF
waf.def: Web application firewall: it filters malicious web requests before they reach the site.

cdn.name: CDN
cdn.def: Network of servers serving your site close to visitors and absorbing part of the attacks.

whois.name: WHOIS
whois.def: Registration directory of a domain: registrar, creation and expiry dates, DNS servers.

rdap.name: RDAP
rdap.def: Modern successor of WHOIS, answering in a structured format.

open_port.name: Port ouvert
open_port.def: A server door that accepts connections. Every open port is a potential attack surface.

banner.name: Bannière
banner.def: Text a service returns on connection, often with its name and version.

typosquatting.name: Typosquatting
typosquatting.def: Domains almost identical to yours (typos) registered to trick your visitors.

dnsbl.name: DNSBL
dnsbl.def: DNS-queried blocklist of IP addresses with a bad reputation (spam, malware).

osint.name: OSINT
osint.def: Open-source intelligence: information obtained from public sources only.

passive.name: Module passif
passive.def: Reads public sources without sending any probe to the target.

active.name: Module actif
active.def: Sends requests or connections to the target. Reserve it for your own domains.

proxy.name: Proxy
proxy.def: Intermediary through which HTTP requests go. DNS does not go through DomainRecon's proxy.

sarif.name: SARIF
sarif.def: Standard format for exchanging security analysis results, read by GitHub and many tools.

help.title: Help
help.lead: Everything to get started: the five-step guide, scan profiles, the legal framework, frequently asked questions and the glossary.

1.title: Enter a domain
1.text: On "New scan", type the domain to analyze (example.com) or paste its address.

2.title: Pick a profile
2.text: Quick for a first look, Full for everything passive, Custom to choose the modules.

3.title: Follow the analysis
3.text: Modules run live. You can cancel at any time.

4.title: Read the result
4.text: The grade sums up the security state. Each finding explains what it is, why it matters and how to fix it.

5.title: Track over time
5.text: Compare two scans, export a report or monitor the domain to be alerted of any change.

profileDesc.rapide: The essential passive modules: a few seconds, no probe sent to the target.
profileDesc.complet: Every passive module plus those that use a configured API key. No active or sensitive module.
profileDesc.personnalise: You choose the modules family by family. The only profile that allows active and sensitive modules.

legal.intro: DomainRecon is an audit tool for your own domains. Querying public sources is free, but probing a system without permission can be an offense.
legal.own: Only analyze domains you own or for which you have written permission from the holder.
legal.active: Active modules send requests and connections to the target (ports, files, HTTP methods): they leave traces in its logs.
legal.sensitive: Sensitive modules look for leaks, exposed files or exploitable weaknesses: they require your explicit authorization.
legal.responsibility: By ticking "I am authorized to test this target" you declare you have that right and take responsibility for it.
legal.note: Rules vary by country. When in doubt, ask the holder's agreement or a lawyer.

1.a: Locally, in the data folder shown in Settings. No result is sent to a DomainRecon server.

2.a: An API-key module is skipped until its key is set in Settings, and an active or sensitive module requires your authorization.

3.a: The module could not conclude (timeout, unreachable service). It is not a good grade: run the scan again.

4.a: Each family has a scale. The score detail, penalties and coverage are visible in the "Score detail" tab of the result.

5.q: Does DNS go through my proxy?
5.a: No. The HTTP or SOCKS proxy only applies to web requests: DNS lookups leave directly from this machine.

6.a: Add a watch, pick the rules and channels, then install the system task so it runs even when the app is closed.

7.q: How do I import an old database?
7.a: In Settings, under "Import an old database": choose the .db file and its scans are imported without duplicates.

8.q: Why does the PDF not generate?
8.a: The PDF uses Playwright's Chromium browser. If it is not installed, use the HTML or Markdown export.

welcome.title: Welcome to DomainRecon
welcome.text: DomainRecon audits the public security of your own domains: DNS, certificates, email, web and reputation. Everything stays on your machine.
welcome.authorized: Authorized use only: only scan your own domains or domains whose owner has given you written permission.
welcome.tour: A short guided tour shows you the parts of the interface, one by one.
welcome.replay: You can restart it at any time from Help or the command palette (Ctrl+K).

tour.keys: Left and right arrows to move, Esc to leave.

palette.title: Quick search
palette.text: This button opens the command palette: type a page name, a domain to scan or a recent scan, then Enter. Shortcut: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac), from any screen.

domain.title: Domain to analyze
domain.text: Type a domain name (for example example.com) or a web address, then click Scan. The analysis runs live and can be cancelled at any time.

profiles.title: Scan profile
profiles.text: The profile picks the modules that run:
profiles.point1: Quick: the essential passive checks, in a few seconds.
profiles.point2: Full: every passive check and those whose API key is set.
profiles.point3: Custom: you tick the modules. Active modules, which send requests to the target, require ticking the authorization box: only tick it for your own domains or with written permission.

nav.title: Navigation menu
nav.text: The screens to follow your domains over time:
nav.point1: Dashboard: the overview of your domains and their grades.
nav.point2: History: every past scan, to reopen or delete.
nav.point3: Batch: several domains analyzed at once.
nav.point4: Compare: two scans side by side, to see what changed.
nav.point5: Monitoring: regular scans and an alert when something changes.

settings.title: Settings
settings.text: Adapt the application to your needs:
settings.point1: API keys, optional: they enable extra modules, the tool works without them.

help.title: Help and glossary
help.text: Step-by-step guide, profiles, legal framework, frequently asked questions and a glossary of technical terms. You can restart this tour from there at any time.

resultScore.title: Security grade
resultScore.text: The grade, from A to F, and the score sum up the state of the domain. Coverage shows the share of checks that could be measured.

resultFinding.title: Findings
resultFinding.text: The most important findings come first. “Understand and fix” explains what it is, why it matters and how to fix it.

resultFamily.title: Check families
resultFamily.text: Each row groups a family (DNS, email, web, TLS…) with its state. Open it for the module-by-module detail.

resultExport.title: Actions and export
resultExport.text: Scan again, follow how the domain changes over time, or click Export to get a PDF, HTML, Markdown, CSV, JSON or SARIF report.

resultIntro.title: Result screen
resultIntro.text: After your first scan, the result screen shows:
resultIntro.point1: The grade from A to F and the score, with the coverage of the checks.
resultIntro.point2: The findings, each with “Understand and fix”.
resultIntro.point3: The check families (DNS, email, web…), to open for the detail.
resultIntro.point4: The Export button: PDF, HTML, Markdown, CSV, JSON or SARIF report.

uninstall.title: Completely uninstall DomainRecon
uninstall.text: Deletes from this machine the scan history, screenshots, API keys and their encryption key, settings, logs and the monitoring task, then removes the program according to your installation. A backup is offered first.

plan.intro: These items will be deleted from this machine:
plan.empty: No DomainRecon data found on this machine.
plan.removeProgram: Also delete the program after closing
plan.removeProgramHint: Only DomainRecon files are erased; the folder is removed only if it is empty.

kind.database: Database (history, monitors, settings, encrypted API keys)
kind.other_data: Other file in the data folder

backup.intro: Before deleting everything, keep a copy of your history, monitors and settings. The .db file can be imported with "Import an old database" in a future installation.

confirm.intro: This action is permanent: nothing can be recovered without a backup. Type {{word}} to confirm.
confirm.label: Type {{word}}

result.failed: Some items are still in use or protected: see the remaining steps.

remaining.windows_uninstaller: On closing, the Windows uninstaller removes the program, its shortcuts and its entry in "Installed apps".
remaining.apt_remove: Remove the program in a terminal (administrator rights):
remaining.delete_program: Delete the program by hand after closing: {{path}}
remaining.program_scheduled: The program will be deleted after closing: {{path}}
remaining.source_tree: Run from source: the project folder is left untouched ({{path}}).
remaining.shared_browsers: Playwright's Chromium, shared with other tools, is not deleted.
remaining.custom_data_dir: Custom data folder (DATA_DIR): only DomainRecon files are removed from {{path}}.
remaining.unsafe_data_dir: Data folder refused for safety, nothing is deleted in it: {{path}}
remaining.external_database: Database outside the data folder, to delete by hand: {{path}}
remaining.external_database_url: External database (DATABASE_URL): delete it with your database tools.
remaining.leftovers_scheduled: Files still in use will be deleted after closing.
remaining.leftovers: Some files could not be deleted: erase them by hand after closing.
